title: cost-probe-sidecar: lightweight sampling + hash-based quant presets
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add cost-probe sidecar for lightweight request sampling; Introduce hash-based quant presets to create stable, reproducible default quant profiles per workload; New CLI snapshotter to capture sample sets for offline profiling; Telemetry and dashboards for sampling coverage and preset regressions.
description: Motivation: Serving cost defaults (batching, caching, quant profiles) need low-friction, workload-aware sampling so Optimize can recommend safe defaults without heavy offline profiling. This PR introduces a lightweight sidecar that runs per-serving-pod and emits compact sampled transaction fingerprints (hash-based signatures) plus short context windows. The sidecar is intentionally low-overhead: sampling rate defaults to 0.2% of requests, configurable by route and model. The sidecar feeds two downstream components: 1) a snapshot CLI + upload path for offline profiling runs, and 2) the quant-preset generator which uses collision-resistant workload hashes to produce reproducible quantization presets tied to stable traffic fingerprints. Key outcomes: safe, reproducible defaults; smaller profiling surface for offline evaluation; and faster rollout of quant profiles with rollback signals. Implementation notes: - Added a new binary cmd/rdw-cost-probe which can run as a sidecar or as a one-shot collector. - Sampling policy implements stratified sampling by input length and route, with deterministic hash-based sampling to avoid cold-start bias. - Quant presets are generated by hashing a compact signature (model, input-shape-bucket, prefix-token-signature) and consulting a policy table (cfg/quant_presets/hashed_defaults.yaml). The generator produces candidate quant profiles plus a stability score used by Optimize for rollout gating. - Telemetry: new metrics exported to prometheus (rdw_probe.sampled_requests, rdw_probe.hash_collisions, rdw_probe.preset_applied, rdw_probe.preset_regression_alerts) and two grafana dashboards in observability/dashboards/cost-probe. - CLI: rdw-cost-snapshot supports local snapshot creation (JSONL) and secure upload to an S3-compatible bucket for the profiler team. - Tests: unit tests for hash stability, integration test harness that runs the sidecar with a small local server and asserts sampling distribution. Rollout plan: feature gated behind --cost-probe-enable and controlled via a feature flag; start canary on internal staging for two weeks, then enable for canary Dedicated clusters, finally make it generally available. Backwards compatibility: sidecar only reads runtime info and emits telemetry; it does not change request paths or model execution. The quant presets are advisory until explicitly applied by Optimize or an operator. This PR also adds a small documentation page and quickstart in docs/optimize/cost-probe.md.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice incremental design. Two asks: 1) include a safety cutoff for sampling so noisy endpoints can't flood metrics, and 2) clarify collision handling in the signature algorithm.

Author (Asha): Added a max_samples_per_minute circuit and updated signature.go to include a 64-bit salt + fnv64 + sha256 fallback. Also added a unit test that asserts <1e-6 collision probability on sampled synthetic workload.
Jordan Lee: Please add an e2e that exercises the snapshot->profiler path (even if it's a small smoke test). Also suggest exposing an opt-in metric with tags for route/model so SRE can run queries.

Author (Asha): Added a minimal e2e smoke test (integration/tests) that runs the sidecar with an in-memory uploader, and added labeled metrics; default labels are minimal to avoid PII (model_id, route_id).
Priya Nair: Docs look good. One editorial nit: expand the rollout steps to explicitly require canary perf check within 72 hours before broader rollout.
Author (Asha): Updated docs and release notes to include the 72-hour canary gating requirement.

notes: This PR intentionally keeps the sampling default conservative (0.2%) to limit telemetry costs. Operators can raise the sample rate per-route after assessing storage/throughput impact.
Quant presets produced by the hashed_defaults table are advisory. We will add an 'auto-apply' toggle in a follow-up PR after three successful canary rollouts.
Follow-ups: telemetry alert that fires on >0.1% collision rate across 24h (ENG-8011), and an Optimize UI card to preview suggested presets (PM-2090).
